diagrams.alt: Adding a b child to node A leaves node B empty because each node owns a separate child dictionary.
Inserting bet beside bee reuses the b and e edges, adds a t child, and marks only the new word ending.
A trie storing bee contains bee but not its unmarked prefix be, the missing word bo, or the empty word.
A trie storing bee has paths for be, bee, and the empty prefix, but no path for bo.
A sorted traversal below be returns be itself, then bee and bet, without changing the trie.
Deleting map prunes its p edge while preserving the shared m and a path to mat.
Three terminal nodes below be count the distinct words be, bee, and bet; duplicate insertion does not increase the count.
Autocomplete for be with limit two reports three matches but displays only be and bee; deleting bee preserves be and bet.
The lowest set bit of 12 is 4; subtracting lowbits visits boundaries 12, 8, and zero.
Fenwick size four allocates five zero cells, reserving cell zero and giving the remaining cells different half-open blocks.
Adding seven at public position two updates internal cells three and four, then stops at cursor eight.
Fenwick prefix 7 visits cells 7, 6, and 4, whose sums 5, 9, and 14 total 28.
For values 6, negative 3, 8, and 2, prefix totals 11 and 6 subtract to give range sum 5 for positions 1 through 2.
Adding each of 6, negative 3, 8, and 2 into an empty Fenwick tree produces internal cells 0, 6, 3, 8, and 13.
Three values occupy leaves four through six of a capacity-four tree; leaf seven is zero padding and parents remain unbuilt.
Combining leaves 6, negative 3, 8, and zero padding builds parent sums 3 and 8, then root sum 11.
The segment query from 1 to 4 combines the leaf value 8 with the adjacent block sum 7 to return 15.
Replacing negative 3 with 5 changes leaf five, its parent to 11, and the root to 19, leaving other branches unchanged.
A minimum tree uses infinity for its padded leaf; the interval from 1 to 3 returns negative 3, and an empty interval returns infinity.
